interview_tips.observation: When asked about the planning module, you provided a clear example (cancel subscription before refund) but could have led with the key metric (18% to 4% reduction) to immediately grab attention.
interview_tips.suggestion: Start your answers with the most impactful result or metric, then provide context. For example: 'We reduced stuck-in-loop rate from 18% to 4% by switching from ReAct to plan-and-execute. The key insight was...'

interview_tips.observation: You mentioned considering alternatives (hierarchical agent, reflection-based ReAct) but didn't discuss the tradeoffs in detail. The interviewer asked about alternatives, and you provided a brief comparison.
interview_tips.suggestion: When discussing alternatives, explicitly state the tradeoffs (e.g., 'Hierarchical was too slow for real-time use, reflection-based was less accurate, so plan-and-execute was the best balance of speed and accuracy'). This demonstrates deeper decision-making.

interview_tips.observation: You mentioned stakeholders (VP of Engineering, support team lead) but didn't elaborate on how you communicated the decision or addressed their concerns beyond latency.
interview_tips.suggestion: When discussing stakeholder buy-in, describe your communication strategy: 'I created a one-pager comparing the three approaches on latency, accuracy, and cost, then walked them through the data. This helped them see the tradeoffs clearly.'

interview_tips.observation: Your pace was generally good, but you occasionally paused or restarted sentences (e.g., 'The thing that pulled me in is the gap...'). This can make you seem less confident.
interview_tips.suggestion: Practice answering common behavioral questions with a timer. Focus on speaking in complete sentences without filler words. Record yourself and listen for hesitations.
